questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Upward accelerating lift cable tension and floor normal reaction

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Upward accelerating lift cable tension and floor normal reaction

hints: For the whole system, use $T - (M + m)g = (M + m)a$. For the crate alone, use $R - mg = ma$.

walkthrough.text:
Consider the whole system (lift plus crate) of total mass $600 + 200 = 800\text{ kg}$ accelerating upwards at $1.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T - (M + m)g = (M + m)a \implies T - 800(10) = 800(1.2)$$
$$T - 8000 = 960 \implies T = 8960\text{ N}$$

Consider the crate of mass $200\text{ kg}$ alone, acted on by upward normal reaction $R$ and downward weight $mg$:
$$R - mg = ma \implies R - 200(10) = 200(1.2)$$
$$R - 2000 = 240 \implies R = 2240\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
When the lift accelerates upwards, the cable must support both the weight of the combined system and supply the net accelerating force:
$$T = (M + m)(g + a) = 800(10 + 1.2) = 800(11.2) = 8960\text{ N}$$

Similarly, the floor pushes up on the crate with greater force than the crate's static weight:
$$R = m(g + a) = 200(10 + 1.2) = 200(11.2) = 2240\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms equation of motion for whole system $T - 800(10) = 800(1.2)$ to find cable tension $T = 8960\text{ N}$.
Applies Newton's second law to the crate alone ($R - 2000 = 200(1.2)$) to find normal reaction $R = 2240\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Downward descending lift decelerating to rest

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Downward descending lift decelerating to rest

hints: Decelerating while moving downwards means the acceleration is directed upwards ($a = +1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ upwards). Use $T - W = Ma$ and $R - mg = ma$.

walkthrough.text:
Since the lift is moving downwards and slowing down, its acceleration is directed vertically upwards with magnitude $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$. For the whole system of mass $430 + 70 = 500\text{ kg}$:
$$T - (M + m)g = (M + m)a \implies T - 500(10) = 500(1.5)$$
$$T - 5000 = 750 \implies T = 5750\text{ N}$$

For the passenger of mass $70\text{ kg}$, resolve vertically upwards:
$$R - mg = ma \implies R - 70(10) = 70(1.5)$$
$$R - 700 = 105 \implies R = 805\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
A downward journey that is braking requires an upward net force. Both cable tension and floor reaction will exceed their static values:
$$T = (430 + 70)(10 + 1.5) = 500(11.5) = 5750\text{ N}$$

The passenger feels heavier under upward acceleration during braking:
$$R = 70(10 + 1.5) = 70(11.5) = 805\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies upward acceleration $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and forms $T - 500(10) = 500(1.5)$ to obtain cable tension $T = 5750\text{ N}$.
Applies Newton's second law to the passenger ($R - 700 = 70(1.5)$) to find normal reaction $R = 805\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Inferring downward acceleration from normal reaction

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Inferring downward acceleration from normal reaction

hints: Write the downward equation of motion for the crate: $mg - R = ma$. Then use $(M + m)g - T = (M + m)a$ for the entire system.

walkthrough.text:
Write Newton's second law for the crate of mass $40\text{ kg}$ resolving vertically downwards:
$$mg - R = ma \implies 40(10) - 320 = 40a$$
$$400 - 320 = 40a \implies 80 = 40a \implies a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

For the whole system of mass $360 + 40 = 400\text{ kg}$ accelerating downwards at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$(M + m)g - T = (M + m)a \implies 400(10) - T = 400(2)$$
$$4000 - T = 800 \implies T = 3200\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
The reduced normal reaction ($320\text{ N} < 400\text{ N}$) indicates downward acceleration. Find $a$ from the difference:
$$a = \frac{mg - R}{m} = \frac{400 - 320}{40} = \frac{80}{40} = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply the downward acceleration to the total mass to find the cable tension:
$$T = (M + m)(g - a) = 400(10 - 2) = 400(8) = 3200\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $mg - R = ma$ to the crate ($400 - 320 = 40a$) to obtain downward acceleration $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies Newton's second law to the total mass ($4000 - T = 400(2)$) to obtain cable tension $T = 3200\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Suspended mass inside lift under upward and downward acceleration

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Suspended mass inside lift under upward and downward acceleration

hints: For upward acceleration, $T_{\text{up}} - mg = ma$. For downward acceleration, $mg - T_{\text{down}} = ma$.

walkthrough.text:
For the suspended block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ accelerating upwards, write Newton's second law:
$$T_{\text{up}} - mg = ma \implies 65 - 5(10) = 5a$$
$$65 - 50 = 5a \implies 15 = 5a \implies a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

When the lift accelerates downwards at $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$, write the downward equation of motion for the block:
$$mg - T_{\text{down}} = ma \implies 5(10) - T_{\text{down}} = 5(3)$$
$$50 - T_{\text{down}} = 15 \implies T_{\text{down}} = 50 - 15 = 35\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
A suspended object behaves symmetrically to an object resting on a scale. Find upward acceleration:
$$a = \frac{T_{\text{up}} - mg}{m} = \frac{65 - 50}{5} = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

When accelerating downward at the same rate, tension drops below weight by the exact same amount:
$$T_{\text{down}} = m(g - a) = 5(10 - 3) = 5(7) = 35\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms equation $T - mg = ma$ ($65 - 50 = 5a$) to obtain upward acceleration $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies $mg - T = ma$ with $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find string tension $T = 35\text{ N}$ when accelerating downwards.

walkthrough.text:

$$R - mg = ma \implies R - 80(10) = 80(1.5)$$
$$R - 800 = 120 \implies R = 920\text{ N}$$

While moving at constant speed, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). Write equilibrium along the vertical:
$$R - mg = 0 \implies R = mg = 80(10) = 800\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Scales measure the normal contact force supporting the body. During upward acceleration, apparent weight increases:
$$R = m(g + a) = 80(10 + 1.5) = 80(11.5) = 920\text{ N}$$

At steady speed, net vertical force is zero, so the scale displays true static weight:
$$R = mg = 80(10) = 800\text{ N}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Cable tension limit, maximum acceleration, and kinematics

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Cable tension limit, maximum acceleration, and kinematics

hints: Set $T_{\text{max}} - Mg = M a_{\text{max}}$ to find maximum acceleration, then use $v = u + at$ with $u = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply Newton's second law vertically upwards with maximum cable tension $T_{\text{max}} = 15000\text{ N}$ and total mass $M = 1200\text{ kg}$:
$$T_{\text{max}} - Mg = M a_{\text{max}} \implies 15000 - 1200(10) = 1200 a_{\text{max}}$$
$$15000 - 12000 = 1200 a_{\text{max}} \implies 3000 = 1200 a_{\text{max}} \implies a_{\text{max}} = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the speed achieved from rest ($u = 0$) after $t = 3\text{ s}$ with acceleration $a = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v = u + at = 0 + 2.5(3) = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
The excess tension above total weight provides the accelerating force:
$$F_{\text{net}} = 15000 - 12000 = 3000\text{ N}$$
$$a_{\text{max}} = \frac{3000}{1200} = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use simple kinematics to find the final speed:
$$v = at = 2.5(3) = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $T_{\text{max}} - Mg = M a_{\text{max}}$ ($15000 - 12000 = 1200a$) to find maximum acceleration $a_{\text{max}} = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies $v = at$ with $a = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$ to obtain speed $v = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Easy: Stacked crates on lift floor with internal contact forces

hints: Isolate crate $A$ alone ($m = 30\text{ kg}$) to find the contact force $R_{BA}$.
To find the floor reaction on $B$, you can either treat $A$ and $B$ together as an $80\text{ kg}$ system, or write the equation of motion for $B$ alone.

walkthrough.text:
Isolate crate $A$ of mass $30\text{ kg}$. The forces acting on $A$ are upward contact force $R_{BA}$ and downward weight $30(10) = 300\text{ N}$:
$$R_{BA} - m_A g = m_A a \implies R_{BA} - 30(10) = 30(1.4)$$
$$R_{BA} - 300 = 42 \implies R_{BA} = 342\text{ N}$$

Consider both crates $A$ and $B$ together as a single load of mass $30 + 50 = 80\text{ kg}$ resting on the floor. The upward force from the floor is $R_{\text{floor}}$:
$$R_{\text{floor}} - (m_A + m_B)g = (m_A + m_B)a \implies R_{\text{floor}} - 80(10) = 80(1.4)$$
$$R_{\text{floor}} - 800 = 112 \implies R_{\text{floor}} = 912\text{ N}$$

Verify by isolating crate $B$ of mass $50\text{ kg}$ alone: upward force $R_{\text{floor}}$, downward weight $500\text{ N}$, and downward reaction from $A$ of magnitude $342\text{ N}$:
$$R_{\text{floor}} - 500 - 342 = 50(1.4) \implies R_{\text{floor}} - 842 = 70 \implies R_{\text{floor}} = 912\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Isolate the top crate first. Only $B$ pushes up on $A$:
$$R_{BA} = m_A(g + a) = 30(10 + 1.4) = 30(11.4) = 342\text{ N}$$

For the floor reaction, the floor must accelerate both crates ($80\text{ kg}$ total):
$$R_{\text{floor}} = (m_A + m_B)(g + a) = 80(11.4) = 912\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies Newton's second law to crate $A$ alone: $R_{BA} - 300 = 30(1.4)$ to find contact force $R_{BA} = 342\text{ N}$.
Considers combined crates ($80\text{ kg}$) or sets up $R_{\text{floor}} - 500 - 342 = 50(1.4)$ for crate $B$ alone.
Solves to obtain contact force of the floor on crate $B$: $R_{\text{floor}} = 912\text{ N}$.

hints: Total mass is $M_{\text{total}} = 600 + 80 = 680\text{ kg}$.
Stage 1 has $a = +1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, Stage 2 has $a = 0$, and Stage 3 has $a = -1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Apply $T - M_{\text{total}}g = M_{\text{total}}a$ in each stage.

walkthrough.text:
Total mass is $M = 600 + 80 = 680\text{ kg}$. For Stage 1 (upward acceleration $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$T_1 - Mg = Ma \implies T_1 - 680(10) = 680(1.5)$$
$$T_1 - 6800 = 1020 \implies T_1 = 7820\text{ N}$$

For Stage 2 (constant speed, $a = 0$):
$$T_2 - Mg = 0 \implies T_2 = Mg = 680(10) = 6800\text{ N}$$

For Stage 3 (upward deceleration, $a = -1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$T_3 - Mg = Ma \implies T_3 - 680(10) = 680(-1.5)$$
$$T_3 - 6800 = -1020 \implies T_3 = 5780\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
The cable tension directly reflects the sign of acceleration across the three phases:
$$T_1 = 680(10 + 1.5) = 680(11.5) = 7820\text{ N}$$
$$T_2 = 680(10) = 6800\text{ N}$$
$$T_3 = 680(10 - 1.5) = 680(8.5) = 5780\text{ N}$$

Notice the symmetry: tension is elevated by $1020\text{ N}$ during acceleration and reduced by $1020\text{ N}$ during deceleration:
$$\Delta T = \pm Ma = \pm 680(1.5) = \pm 1020\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $T_1 - 6800 = 680(1.5)$ to find Stage 1 tension $T_1 = 7820\text{ N}$.
Identifies $a = 0$ in Stage 2 to obtain tension $T_2 = 6800\text{ N}$.
Applies $T_3 - 6800 = 680(-1.5)$ to find Stage 3 tension $T_3 = 5780\text{ N}$.

$$8120 = 11.6(M + 120) \implies M + 120 = \frac{8120}{11.6} = 700\text{ kg}$$
$$M = 700 - 120 = 580\text{ kg}$$

Now compute tension during downward acceleration:
$$T_1 = M_{\text{total}}(g - a_1) = 700(10 - 0.8) = 700(9.2) = 6440\text{ N}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core Medium: Counterweight lift system with internal box reaction and kinematics

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Medium: Counterweight lift system with internal box reaction and kinematics

hints: Total mass of lift and box is $320 + 80 = 400\text{ kg}$.
Counterweight $B$ has mass $600\text{ kg}$ and descends, so $m_B g - T = m_B a$.
For the lift system ascending, $T - m_A g = m_A a$. Add to solve for $a$ and find $T$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the combined mass of the ascending lift system:
$$m_{\text{lift}} = 320 + 80 = 400\text{ kg}$$
Write the equations of motion for descending counterweight $B$ ($600\text{ kg}$) and ascending lift system ($400\text{ kg}$):
$$\text{For } B: \quad 600(10) - T = 600a \implies 6000 - T = 600a$$
$$\text{For lift system}: \quad T - 400(10) = 400a \implies T - 4000 = 400a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and solve for acceleration $a$:
$$(6000 - T) + (T - 4000) = 600a + 400a \implies 2000 = 1000a \implies a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into either equation of motion to find tension $T$:
$$T = 4000 + 400(2) = 4000 + 800 = 4800\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Treat the lift and its contents as a single package of mass $400\text{ kg}$. The net gravitational driving force acts on the total mass of $1000\text{ kg}$:
$$a = \frac{m_B g - m_{\text{lift}} g}{m_B + m_{\text{lift}}} = \frac{6000 - 4000}{600 + 400} = \frac{2000}{1000} = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Find cable tension using the descending counterweight:
$$T = m_B(g - a) = 600(10 - 2) = 600(8) = 4800\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms equations of motion $6000 - T = 600a$ and $T - 4000 = 400a$ for the connected system.
Solves to obtain acceleration $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Substitutes $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find cable tension $T = 4800\text{ N}$.

$$R - 800 = 160 \implies R = 960\text{ N}$$

$$R = m(g + a) = 80(10 + 2) = 80(12) = 960\text{ N}$$

Use kinematic formula to determine speed at $2.25\text{ m}$:

hints: Parcel $P$ acts as an internal accelerometer: write $T_P - m_P g = m_P a$ vertically upwards.
Substitute $T_P = 96\text{ N}$, $m_P = 8\text{ kg}$, and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find the upward acceleration $a$.
Write Newton's second law for crate $Q$ of mass $52\text{ kg}$ on the floor: $R_Q - m_Q g = m_Q a$.
Calculate the total mass $M_{\text{total}} = 400 + 8 + 52 = 460\text{ kg}$ and use $T_{\text{cable}} - M_{\text{total}}g = M_{\text{total}}a$.

walkthrough.text:
For parcel $P$ of mass $8\text{ kg}$ with string tension $T_P = 96\text{ N}$, write Newton's second law vertically upwards:
$$T_P - m_P g = m_P a \implies 96 - 8(10) = 8a$$
$$96 - 80 = 8a \implies 16 = 8a \implies a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

For crate $Q$ of mass $52\text{ kg}$ on the floor accelerating upwards at $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R_Q - m_Q g = m_Q a \implies R_Q - 52(10) = 52(2)$$
$$R_Q - 520 = 104 \implies R_Q = 624\text{ N}$$

For the whole system of total mass $400 + 8 + 52 = 460\text{ kg}$ accelerating upwards at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T_{\text{cable}} - M_{\text{total}}g = M_{\text{total}}a \implies T_{\text{cable}} - 460(10) = 460(2)$$
$$T_{\text{cable}} - 4600 = 920 \implies T_{\text{cable}} = 5520\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use the suspended mass as an accelerometer to read the system acceleration:
$$a = \frac{T_P - m_P g}{m_P} = \frac{96 - 80}{8} = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply this acceleration to crate $Q$ and to the total system mass of $460\text{ kg}$:
$$R_Q = 52(10 + 2) = 624\text{ N}$$
$$T_{\text{cable}} = 460(10 + 2) = 460(12) = 5520\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $96 - 80 = 8a$ to find upward acceleration $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies $R_Q - 520 = 52(2)$ to obtain normal reaction $R_Q = 624\text{ N}$.
Considers total mass $460\text{ kg}$ to obtain cable tension $T_{\text{cable}} = 5520\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Hard: Lift containing suspended parcel and floor crate with acceleration, deceleration, and stopping kinematics

hints: For crate $Q$, write $R_Q - m_Q g = m_Q a$ with $R_Q = 416\text{ N}$ and $m_Q = 52\text{ kg}$.
Solve for $a$ to find the acceleration ($a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, meaning deceleration of $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$).
Use this acceleration in the equation of motion for parcel $P$: $T_P - m_P g = m_P a$ to find string tension $T_P$.
Apply Newton's second law to the total mass of $460\text{ kg}$ to find cable tension $T_{\text{cable}} = 460(g + a)$.

walkthrough.text:
Write Newton's second law vertically upwards for crate $Q$ of mass $52\text{ kg}$:
$$R_Q - m_Q g = m_Q a \implies 416 - 52(10) = 52a$$
$$416 - 520 = 52a \implies -104 = 52a \implies a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Thus the deceleration is $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

For parcel $P$ of mass $8\text{ kg}$ under acceleration $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T_P - m_P g = m_P a \implies T_P - 8(10) = 8(-2)$$
$$T_P - 80 = -16 \implies T_P = 64\text{ N}$$

For the whole system of mass $460\text{ kg}$ during deceleration:
$$T_{\text{cable}} - 460(10) = 460(-2) \implies T_{\text{cable}} - 4600 = -920 \implies T_{\text{cable}} = 3680\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
From the reduced reaction on $Q$, compute the braking deceleration:
$$a = \frac{416 - 520}{52} = -2\text{ m s}^{-2} \implies \text{deceleration } 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Both the string tension and the main cable tension reflect the effective downward inertial reduction:
$$T_P = 8(10 - 2) = 64\text{ N}$$
$$T_{\text{cable}} = 460(10 - 2) = 460(8) = 3680\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $416 - 520 = 52a$ to determine deceleration of magnitude $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies Newton's second law to parcel $P$ with $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find string tension $T_P = 64\text{ N}$.
Applies Newton's second law to total mass $460\text{ kg}$ to obtain cable tension $T_{\text{cable}} = 3680\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Hard: Lift containing suspended parcel and floor crate with acceleration, deceleration, and stopping kinematics

hints: The initial velocity for the deceleration phase is $u = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and the final velocity is $v = 0$.
The acceleration is $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Apply $v = u + at$ to find the time $t$ taken to come to rest.
Apply $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ or $s = \frac{1}{2}(u + v)t$ to find the stopping distance $s$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the time $t$ to come to rest ($v = 0$) from initial speed $u = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with deceleration $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ ($a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$v = u + at \implies 0 = 6 - 2t \implies 2t = 6 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

Calculate the distance $s$ travelled during this deceleration:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as \implies 0^2 = 6^2 + 2(-2)s \implies 0 = 36 - 4s \implies 4s = 36 \implies s = 9\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
At a steady deceleration of $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, shedding $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ takes:
$$t = \frac{u}{|a|} = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ s}$$

The average speed during linear deceleration is half the initial speed:
$$s = v_{\text{avg}} t = \frac{6 + 0}{2} \times 3 = 3 \times 3 = 9\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $0 = 6 - 2t$ to obtain stopping time $t = 3\text{ s}$.
Applies $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ or $s = \frac{u+v}{2}t$ to obtain deceleration distance $s = 9\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Hard: Mine cage descent, cable snap with apparent weightlessness, and emergency braking

hints: Find the total mass of the cage and miners: $M_{\text{total}} = 800 + 400 = 1200\text{ kg}$.
Since the cage is accelerating downwards, downward weight exceeds cable tension: $M_{\text{total}}g - T = M_{\text{total}}a$.
Substitute $M_{\text{total}} = 1200\text{ kg}$ and $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find cable tension $T$.
For the miners alone ($m = 400\text{ kg}$), write the downward equation of motion: $mg - R = ma$ to find normal reaction $R$.

walkthrough.text:
For the total mass $800 + 400 = 1200\text{ kg}$ accelerating downwards at $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, write Newton's second law downwards:
$$(M + m)g - T = (M + m)a \implies 1200(10) - T = 1200(1.5)$$
$$12000 - T = 1800 \implies T = 12000 - 1800 = 10200\text{ N}$$

For the miners of mass $400\text{ kg}$ accelerating downwards at $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$mg - R = ma \implies 400(10) - R = 400(1.5)$$
$$4000 - R = 600 \implies R = 4000 - 600 = 3400\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
While lowering with downward acceleration, the cable holds less than the static weight:
$$T = (M + m)(g - a) = 1200(10 - 1.5) = 1200(8.5) = 10200\text{ N}$$

The miners feel reduced floor reaction:
$$R = m(g - a) = 400(10 - 1.5) = 400(8.5) = 3400\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms downward equation of motion for total mass $1200(10) - T = 1200(1.5)$.
Solves to obtain cable tension $T = 10200\text{ N}$.
Applies $400(10) - R = 400(1.5)$ to find normal reaction on miners $R = 3400\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Hard: Mine cage descent, cable snap with apparent weightlessness, and emergency braking

hints: First calculate the speed $v_1$ reached after $4\text{ s}$ of descent from rest using $v_1 = at = 1.5(4)$.
When the cable breaks, the cage and miners fall freely under gravity with acceleration $a = g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Write Newton's second law for the miners during free fall: $mg - R = mg$, which shows $R = 0\text{ N}$.
Use $v = u + gt$ with $u = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $t = 0.5\text{ s}$ to find speed when brakes engage.

walkthrough.text:
Find the speed of the cage at $t = 4\text{ s}$ just before the cable breaks:
$$v_1 = u + at = 0 + 1.5(4) = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

During free fall, the cage accelerates downwards under gravity alone, so $a = g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$. For the miners:
$$mg - R = ma \implies mg - R = mg \implies R = 0\text{ N}$$
Thus the contact force between the miners and the floor is zero (apparent weightlessness).

Calculate the downward speed $v_2$ of the cage after falling freely for $t = 0.5\text{ s}$ from initial speed $u = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$v_2 = u + gt = 6 + 10(0.5) = 6 + 5 = 11\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine the initial speed at the cable break event:
$$v_1 = 1.5(4) = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

When in free fall, both the cage and the miners accelerate at $g$. The floor does not push on the miners at all:
$$R = m(g - g) = 0\text{ N}$$
Then calculate speed after $0.5\text{ s}$ of free fall:
$$v_2 = 6 + 10(0.5) = 11\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds speed at $t = 4\text{ s}$ using $v = 1.5(4) = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Shows that during free fall $a = g$ leads to $R = m(g - g) = 0\text{ N}$.
Applies $v = u + gt$ ($6 + 10(0.5)$) to find speed at brake engagement $v = 11\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Hard: Mine cage descent, cable snap with apparent weightlessness, and emergency braking

hints: Total downward weight is $(800 + 400)g = 12000\text{ N}$. Net upward force is $B - W = 18000 - 12000 = 6000\text{ N}$.
Find upward acceleration $a = 6000 / 1200 = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 11\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v = 0$ to find stopping distance.
For miners, write $R - mg = ma$ with $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ upwards.

walkthrough.text:
Consider the whole system of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ under upward braking force $18000\text{ N}$ and downward weight $1200(10) = 12000\text{ N}$. Resolve upwards:
$$\Sigma F_{\text{up}} = B - Mg = 18000 - 12000 = 6000\text{ N}$$
$$6000 = 1200 a_{\text{brake}} \implies a_{\text{brake}} = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Thus the downward motion decelerates at $5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Calculate the stopping distance $s_3$ from speed $u = 11\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to rest ($v = 0$) under deceleration $5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ ($a = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ downwards):
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as \implies 0^2 = 11^2 + 2(-5)s_3$$
$$0 = 121 - 10s_3 \implies 10s_3 = 121 \implies s_3 = 12.1\text{ m}$$

For the miners of mass $400\text{ kg}$ during upward braking acceleration $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R - mg = ma \implies R - 400(10) = 400(5)$$
$$R - 4000 = 2000 \implies R = 6000\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the net upward braking force and resulting deceleration:
$$a = \frac{18000 - 1200(10)}{1200} = \frac{6000}{1200} = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Determine the stopping distance from $11\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s = \frac{u^2}{2|a|} = \frac{11^2}{2(5)} = \frac{121}{10} = 12.1\text{ m}$$

The miners feel heavy as the emergency brakes decelerate their fall:
$$R = m(g + a) = 400(10 + 5) = 400(15) = 6000\text{ N}$$
